written.q: Explain the black-box problem and the three goals of explainable AI with an example for each.
written.a: Modern ML prioritises predictive performance over transparency; complex models hide decision logic in millions of parameters, which is risky in medicine (life safety), credit scoring (financial loss) and driving (legal liability). XAI goals: Trust (verify legitimate logic, e.g. a husky vs wolf model that actually looked at snow); Debugging (find where, how and why systematic errors occur on edge cases, e.g. failures on older patients); Fairness and auditing (check decisions do not discriminate on protected attributes, e.g. a hiring tool using gender or a stand-in).

written.q: Describe the accuracy vs interpretability trade-off and how glass-box models and post-hoc methods fit in.
written.a: Glass-box models (linear / logistic regression, decision trees) have very high interpretability and moderate power; ensembles (random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM) moderate and high; deep learning (CNNs, transformers) low and very high. Glass-box models explain themselves (coefficients, IF-THEN rules). When we need a black box, post-hoc methods such as permutation importance, LIME and SHAP explain it afterwards.

written.q: Distinguish global and local interpretability and say which methods suit each.
written.a: Global explains the overall logic across the dataset (which features drive predictions overall): permutation importance, averaged SHAP. Local explains one prediction (why was this loan rejected?): LIME and SHAP. Global suits engineers and auditors; local suits the affected person.

written.q: A model has baseline accuracy 90 %. Shuffling hours studied gives 62 %, attendance 80 %, shoe size 90 %. Compute and interpret the permutation importances.
written.a: Importance = baseline − shuffled accuracy: hours 28, attendance 10, shoe size 0. The model relied heavily on hours studied, somewhat on attendance and ignored shoe size. Caveats: it is global, works with any model, and correlated features can hide each other.

written.q: Explain LIME and compute the local slope for f(x) = x² at x = 3 using points 2.9 and 3.1.
written.a: LIME fits a simple interpretable model (such as a line) to the complex model's predictions for many perturbed copies near one point, weighting nearer copies more; the coefficients are the explanation. f(2.9) = 8.41, f(3.1) = 9.61; slope = (9.61 − 8.41)/0.2 = 6, so near x = 3 each +1 in x raises the output by about 6. It is valid only locally (at x = 0 the true slope is 0).

written.q: Explain SHAP and compute the values for Income and Debt given baseline 50, Income only 70, Debt only 60, both 90. State its two axioms.
written.a: SHAP uses Shapley values: each feature's average marginal contribution over all orders (coalitions). Income: first adds 20, after Debt adds 30, average 25. Debt: first adds 10, after Income adds 20, average 15. 25 + 15 = 40 = 90 − 50. Axioms: consistency (if a feature's contribution increases or stays the same its SHAP value does not decrease) and additivity (contributions sum to prediction minus baseline). Cost grows as 2n.

written.q: List the nine ethical foundations of (Gen)AI and explain how XAI supports three of them.
written.a: Integrity, originality, transparency, accountability, compliance, security, intellectual property, fairness and bias, human oversight. XAI supports transparency and accountability (you can only be accountable for what you can explain), fairness (SHAP can reveal reliance on a protected attribute) and human oversight (humans can only supervise decisions they understand).

written.q: Summarise the EU AI Act's risk levels with examples, the duties of high-risk systems and the maximum fines.
written.a: Unacceptable risk (banned): social scoring, manipulative AI, untargeted face scraping. High risk: hiring, education, credit scoring, law enforcement, critical infrastructure; duties: risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy / robustness / cybersecurity. Specific transparency (limited) risk: chatbots and deepfakes must be disclosed or labelled. Minimal risk: spam filters, games. GPAI models have documentation, copyright and systemic-risk duties. Fines up to €35 million or 7 % of turnover for prohibited practices, €15 million or 3 % for most other duties, €7.5 million or 1 % for false information.
